== ConAgua/Checker/Pipeline.lean#L69-L72
    69  /-- What every stage may assume of the inputs: a 64-bit platform, both buffers below `2^63`
    70  bytes, every word array below `2^64` words. -/
    71  def InputsOK (b pb : ByteArray) (sz : TieredArray → Nat) : Prop :=
    72    System.Platform.numBits = 64 ∧ b.size < 2 ^ 63 ∧ pb.size < 2 ^ 63 ∧ ∀ s, sz s < 2 ^ 64

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L8-L33
     8  /-!
     9  # The compiler from L to Kraken x64
    10  
    11  See DESIGN.md, "The compiler". One pass: an expression is evaluated straight into its target
    12  register by `gen`, with scratch registers; where `gen` does not apply, into `rax` with
    13  intermediate values in fixed per-frame temporary slots (`compileE`).
    14  
    15  **Machine state during L code.**
    16  * `r15` = `T`, the address of the run's descriptor table (`Tab`); pinned.
    17  * `r14` = the fuel counter; decremented at every loop back-edge and every call.
    18  * `rsp` = the current frame; constant while a body runs. Local `x` is the word at `rsp + 8x`,
    19    temporary `t` is at `rsp + 8(nlocals + t)`. The frame has `frameWords` words.
    20  * `rbp` = the trampoline's saved stack pointer; never written by L code.
    21  * `rbx`, `r12`, `r13`: free; the trampoline saves and restores them for its caller.
    22  * `rax` = expression result, `rcx`/`rdx` = scratch, `rsi` = argument pointer at a call.
    23  
    24  **Exits.** `ca_error`, `ca_abort` and `ca_exhausted` are global; they restore the caller's `rsp`
    25  from `rbp` and return to the harness with `rdx` = 2, 2 resp. 1. `ca_abort` is an error whose code
    26  (`Err.code`) is in `rbx` (`abort e`, `if c abort k`: `if c abort k` sets `rbx` before the test
    27  and keeps its one conditional jump; the test itself keeps `rbx`), `ca_error` one with code `0` (a
    28  bounds check, a bare `abort`); both return the code in `rax`. `abort e` may overwrite any
    29  register, a leaf's locals in `rbx` included (nothing after an abort reads a local), but `if c abort
    30  k` writes `rbx` also when it does not abort: it does so only where no local lives in `rbx`
    31  (`Ctx.rbxFree`, `sim_ifAbortK`); in a leaf that keeps a local there it is the general `if`. A
    32  normal return has `rdx` = 0 and the result in `rax`.
    33  -/

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L1965-L1986
  1965  def trampoline (tab : Tab) (entry : FnName) (c np : Nat) : Program :=
  1966    [.label enterL,
  1967     movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np)) .r15, movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np + 8)) .rbx,
  1968     movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np + 16)) .r12, movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np + 24)) .r13,
  1969     i64 (.push (oR .rbp)), i64 (.push (oR .r14)), i64 (.push (oR .rdi)),
  1970     movRR .rbp .rsp, movRR .r15 .rdi, movRR .r14 .rsi,
  1971     movRM .rsp (mb .r15 Tab.stackTop),
  1972     i64 (.lea (rr .rsi) (mb .r15 tab.args))] ++
  1973    (if np ≤ argRegs.length then loadArgs tab 0 (argRegs.take np) else []) ++ burnFuel ++
  1974    [i64 (.call (.rel (.sub (.label (fnL entry)) .after_current_instruction))),
  1975     jmpL okL,
  1976     .label exhaustedL, movRI .rdx 1, jmpL finishL,
  1977     .label errorL, movRI .rbx 0,
  1978     .label abortL, movRR .rax .rbx, movRI .rdx 2,
  1979     .label finishL, movRR .rsp .rbp,
  1980     i64 (.pop (.reg (rr .r15))),
  1981     movRM .rbx (mb .r15 (tab.save np + 8)), movRM .r12 (mb .r15 (tab.save np + 16)),
  1982     movRM .r13 (mb .r15 (tab.save np + 24)), movRM .r15 (mb .r15 (tab.save np)),
  1983     i64 (.pop (.reg (rr .r14))), i64 (.pop (.reg (rr .rbp))),
  1984     i64 .ret,
  1985     .label okL] ++ loadRes { tab, fn := entry, nl := 0, brk := okL } 0 c (tab.nres - c) ++
  1986    [movRI .rdx 0, jmpL finishL]

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L774
   774  def allocRegs : List Reg64 := [.rdi, .r8, .r9, .r10, .r11, .rsi, .rbx, .r12, .r13]

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L1936-L1948
  1936  def compileFn (tab : Tab) (t sk : NTree) (f : FnName) (fd : FunDecl) : Program :=
  1937    let ctx := fnCtx tab t sk f fd
  1938    let F := fd.nlocals + tempsS ctx.alloc ctx.nr fd.body
  1939    if frameless fd then [.label (fnL f)] ++ fnBody ctx fd ++ [i64 .ret]
  1940    else if ctx.leaf && sk.find (nameCode f) == some F then
  1941    [.label (fnL f), i64 (.sub (.reg (rr .rsp)) (oI (8 * F)))] ++ fnBody ctx fd ++
  1942    [i64 (.add (.reg (rr .rsp)) (oI (8 * F))), i64 .ret]
  1943    else
  1944    [.label (fnL f),
  1945     movRR .rax .rsp, i64 (.sub (.reg (rr .rax)) (oM (mb .r15 Tab.stackLimit))),
  1946     i64 (.cmp (.reg (rr .rax)) (oI (8 * F + 8 + 8 * ctx.need))), jccL .c exhaustedL,
  1947     i64 (.sub (.reg (rr .rsp)) (oI (8 * F)))] ++ fnBody ctx fd ++
  1948    [i64 (.add (.reg (rr .rsp)) (oI (8 * F))), i64 .ret]

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L98-L157
    98  /-- **The layout check**: `l` lists the array at each of the `nb + nw` positions, `m` maps each of
    99  them to its position and nothing else (an entry `k ↦ v` has `v` in range and `l[v]` of code `k`),
   100  the byte positions `[0, nb)` hold tier-0 names, and a tier 1 sits at a word position right after
   101  its tier 0. -/
   102  def layOkB (nb nw : Nat) (l : List TieredArray) (m : NTree) : Bool :=
   103    l.length == nb + nw &&
   104    m.all (fun k v => decide (v < nb + nw) && (l[v]?.map TieredArray.code == some k)) &&
   105    (List.range (nb + nw)).all (fun i => m.find (arrAtD l i).code == some i) &&
   106    (List.range nb).all (fun i => !(arrAtD l i).hi) &&
   107    (List.range (nb + nw)).all (fun i => !(arrAtD l i).hi ||
   108      (decide (nb < i) && arrAtD l (i - 1) == TieredArray.t0 (arrAtD l i).arr))
   109  
   110  /-- The number of result registers. -/
   111  def maxRes : Nat := 6
   112  
   113  /-- The layout of the descriptor table at `T`:
   114  * `[T]` the initial stack pointer (top of the stack region), `[T + 8]` its lower limit;
   115  * `[T + 16 + 8p]` the base of the array at descriptor position `p < nb + nw` (`Tab.dbase`), then
   116    `[T + 16 + 8 (nb + nw) + 8p]` its length (`Tab.dlen`), in bytes for a byte position (`p < nb`),
   117    in words for a word position;
   118  * then the constant data `rom` (the byte strings of the program's `ldc` reads), padded to whole
   119    words;
   120  * then the result area: results `maxRes, maxRes + 1, …, nres - 1` of a call, one word each (empty
   121    if `nres ≤ maxRes`);
   122  * then the global variables `0, …, ng - 1`, one word each;
   123  * then the arguments of the entry function, one word each.
   124  
   125  (`nres` is not part of the table in memory: it says how many results the code passes.) -/
   126  structure Tab where
   127    /-- The byte positions `[0, nb)`. -/
   128    nb : Nat
   129    /-- The word positions `[nb, nb + nw)`. -/
   130    nw : Nat
   131    /-- The array at each position (`Tab.wAt`; a byte array `a` as `↑a`). -/
   132    arrAt : List TieredArray
   133    /-- The layout map: `s.code ↦` the position of `s` (`Tab.pos64`, `Tab.pos8`). -/
   134    lmap : NTree
   135    /-- The map and the position list agree (`layOkB`). -/
   136    layOk : layOkB nb nw arrAt lmap = true
   137    rom : List UInt8 := []
   138    /-- The number of results in use: the most results any `return` gives or any call reads. The
   139    first `maxRes` go in registers (`resReg 0`, …), the rest in the table's result area. -/
   140    nres : Nat := 1
   141    /-- The number of global variables: global `g` (with `g.id < ng`) is the word at `globOff g`. -/
   142    ng : Nat := 0
   143    /-- Minimum lengths (`L.ArrDecl.min`): `(s.code, k)` says that word array `s` has at
   144    least `k` words in every layout the code runs in (`Layout.Ok.min64`; the entry stubs establish
   145    it), so a constant index below `k` needs no bounds check (`Tab.min64`). -/
   146    mins : List (Nat × Nat) := []
   147    /-- The table-relative array (`L.ArrDecl.atTable`): `(a, c)` says that tier 0 of word array `a`
   148    starts at `T + c`, past the table and the trampoline's save area, in every layout the code runs in
   149    (`Layout.Ok.tbl64`; the entry stubs place it there), so the code addresses it from `r15` without
   150    loading its base. -/
   151    tbl : Option (ArrId × Nat) := none
   152    /-- `rom.length`, stored: the offsets past the constant data (`resOff`, `globOff`, `args`) are
   153    then arithmetic on the table's fields, and the kernel does not count the bytes of a large ROM
   154    each time it evaluates the code generator (DESIGN.md, "Kernel-checked compiler output"). -/
   155    romLen : Nat := rom.length
   156    romLen_eq : romLen = rom.length := by rfl
   157    deriving Repr, DecidableEq

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L168-L180
   168  /-- The byte arrays a program may name (a byte position), and their positions. -/
   169  def Tab.dom8 (t : Tab) (a : ArrId) : Bool :=
   170    match t.lmap.find (TieredArray.t0 a).code with
   171    | some p => decide (p < t.nb)
   172    | none => false
   173  def Tab.pos8 (t : Tab) (a : ArrId) : Nat := (t.lmap.find (TieredArray.t0 a).code).getD 0
   174  
   175  /-- The word arrays a program may name (a word position), and their positions. -/
   176  def Tab.dom64 (t : Tab) (s : TieredArray) : Bool :=
   177    match t.lmap.find s.code with
   178    | some p => decide (t.nb ≤ p)
   179    | none => false
   180  def Tab.pos64 (t : Tab) (s : TieredArray) : Nat := (t.lmap.find s.code).getD 0

== ConAgua/Compiler/Step.lean#L11-L19
    11  /-!
    12  # One instruction at a time
    13  
    14  The compiler proof is a forward simulation on Kraken's own judgment
    15  `Eventually (step1 Host.exe) Q ⟨d, pc⟩` ("every run from `d` at `pc` reaches `Q`"), for an
    16  arbitrary `Host` program that contains the compiled code. Each lemma here steps over one
    17  instruction form the compiler emits, in continuation-passing style: the hypothesis is the
    18  `Eventually` at the next state, the conclusion the `Eventually` at this one.
    19  -/

== ConAgua/Compiler/Rel.lean#L144-L164
   144  /-- L's memory `m` in the machine's data memory `d`. The machine side (`Layout`, the table) is
   145  positional; L's arrays are names, related to their regions through the compiler's layout map
   146  (`Tab.pos8`, `Tab.pos64`): the array a program may name (`dom8`, `dom64`) has the region of its
   147  position. -/
   148  structure MemRel (G : Layout) (m : Mem) (d : DataMem) : Prop where
   149    size8 : ∀ a, G.tab.dom8 a → (m.arr8 a).size = G.s (G.tab.pos8 a)
   150    size64 : ∀ s, G.tab.dom64 s → (m.arr64 s).size = G.s (G.tab.pos64 s)
   151    get8 : ∀ a, G.tab.dom8 a → ∀ (i : Nat) (h : i < (m.arr8 a).size),
   152      d.get? (A (G.b (G.tab.pos8 a) + i)) = some (m.arr8 a)[i]
   153    get64 : ∀ s, G.tab.dom64 s → ∀ (i : Nat) (h : i < (m.arr64 s).size),
   154      rdW d (A (G.b (G.tab.pos64 s) + 8 * i)) = some (m.arr64 s)[i]
   155    limit : rdW d (A (G.T + 8)) = some (UInt64.ofNat G.lo)
   156    /-- The descriptors, by position: no L array in them. -/
   157    base : ∀ p < G.tab.nb + G.tab.nw, rdW d (A (G.T + (G.tab.dbase p).toNat)) = some (UInt64.ofNat (G.b p))
   158    len : ∀ p < G.tab.nb + G.tab.nw, rdW d (A (G.T + (G.tab.dlen p).toNat)) = some (UInt64.ofNat (G.s p))
   159    rom : ∀ (i : Nat) (h : i < G.tab.rom.length),
   160      d.get? (A (G.T + 16 + 16 * (G.tab.nb + G.tab.nw) + i)) = some G.tab.rom[i]
   161    stack : ∀ x, G.InStack x → (d.get? (A x)).isSome
   162    res : ∀ x, G.InRes x → (d.get? (A x)).isSome
   163    /-- The global variables. -/
   164    glob : ∀ g : GVar, g.id < G.tab.ng → rdW d (A (G.globAddr g)) = some (m.glob g)

== ConAgua/Compiler/Rel.lean#L71-L85
    71  /-- The regions are inside the address space and pairwise disjoint, every word array the program
    72  may name has at least its minimum length (`Tab.min64`, the hint the code generator drops
    73  constant-index bounds checks by), and the table-relative array (`Tab.tbl64`) starts where the
    74  code addresses it, at `T + c`. -/
    75  structure Ok : Prop where
    76    tab_end : G.tabEnd < 2 ^ 64
    77    hi_le : G.hi < 2 ^ 64
    78    lo_le : G.lo ≤ G.hi
    79    end_ : ∀ p < G.tab.nb + G.tab.nw, G.b p + G.tab.wd p * G.s p < 2 ^ 64
    80    tab_stack : ∀ x, G.InTab x → ¬ G.InStack x
    81    tab_arr : ∀ x, G.InTab x → ¬ G.InArr x
    82    stack_arr : ∀ x, G.InStack x → ¬ G.InArr x
    83    disj : ∀ p < G.tab.nb + G.tab.nw, ∀ q < G.tab.nb + G.tab.nw, p ≠ q → ∀ x, G.In p x → ¬ G.In q x
    84    min64 : ∀ s, G.tab.dom64 s = true → G.tab.min64 s ≤ G.s (G.tab.pos64 s)
    85    tbl64 : ∀ s c, G.tab.dom64 s = true → G.tab.tbl64 s = some c → G.b (G.tab.pos64 s) = G.T + c

== ConAgua/Compiler/Abi.lean#L8-L39
     8  # The entry stubs (lane `abi`)
     9  
    10  The harness's whole job shrinks to: map a zero region, hand over the two input buffers, call
    11  `ca_start(in, in_len, pins, pins_len, base, base_len)` once. `ca_start` is the sequential driver
    12  (`parStub`, below): it calls entry 1 and then entry 2 on the same region. Both go through the
    13  setup stub `ca_setup` (`abiStub`, an internal label; the argument registers as `ca_start`'s),
    14  emitted before the trampoline, which sets up inside the region everything the harness used to lay
    15  out (`L.Compiler.Tab`), then tail-jumps into the trampoline `ca_enter(T, fuel)`:
    16  
    17  * System V arguments: `rdi`/`rsi` = the input bytes (the byte array at descriptor position `0`),
    18    `rdx`/`rcx` = the pin-data bytes (position `1`; ignored if the program has one byte array), `r8` =
    19    `base`, `r9` = `base_len`. Returns `rax`/`rdx` as `ca_enter` does. Which arrays sit at positions
    20    `0` and `1` is the layout map's business: the final theorem's proof checks that they are the
    21    input's and the pin data's (`ConAgua/Final/Abi.lean`).
    22  * If `base_len < abiNeed`, or if `in_len` or `pins_len` is `2^63` or more (the top bit of `rsi`
    23    or `rcx` set: `cmp r, 0; jl`), it returns at once with `rdx = 1` (resources exhausted; never
    24    accept). So a run that gets past the stub has both buffers below `2^63` bytes, which the
    25    refinements assume (`InputsOK`).
    26  * The region is a static partition into `abiSlot`-byte slots (no allocator; the pages that are
    27    never touched never become real): slot `0` is the table (`T = base`), slot `1` the L stack
    28    (`abiStack` bytes at its bottom), then one slot per descriptor position past the two buffers, in
    29    position order (`Tab.slotOf`). Each array starts at its slot's start; its length is `abiSlot`
    30    bytes, resp. `abiWords` words. The table-relative array (`Tab.tbl64`) lies instead inside slot
    31    `0`, past the table, with its minimum length (`abiOff`, `abiSz`); it has the last position, which
    32    gets no slot (`Tab.nslot`).
    33  * The constant data is written into the table by immediate stores (no `.rodata` read); the result
    34    area and the global variables are the region's zeros.
    35  * The fuel is `2^62 - 1` (`compile_correct` takes any `N < 2^62`).
    36  
    37  Nothing here is trusted: `sim_abiStub` (`ConAgua/Compiler/AbiSim.lean`) runs the stub on the
    38  machine, `abiLayout_ok` and `abi_memRel` (`ConAgua/Final/Abi.lean`) show that it establishes
    39  `Layout.Ok`/`MemRel` for the partition, and `abi_harness` gives `compile_correct`'s premises at

    17  /-- **The checker's code**: the `.text` section of `checker.s`. -/
    18  noncomputable def checkerFile : Program := include_asm "../checker.s"

    24  asm_file_eq checkerFile_eq : checkerFile = checkerStub ++ checkerAsm via checkerAsm_eq

== ConAgua/Checker/Asm.lean#L12-L21
    12  /-!
    13  # The checker's machine code, as a kernel-checked literal (generated by `scripts/checker_prog.py`; do not edit)
    14  
    15  `checkerAsm : Program` is the compiled checker as a literal term, and
    16  `checkerAsm_eq : compileProg checkerTab checkerProg "check" = checkerAsm` is checked by the kernel,
    17  one function at a time (`asm_lit`, `ConAgua/Compiler/AsmLit.lean`; the functions' checks are in
    18  `AsmPart0` … `AsmPart9`), so running the compiler as compiled Lean code is not trusted.
    19  `checkerFile_eq` (`ConAgua/Checker/AsmFileEq.lean`) compares it with the committed file
    20  `checker.s` (`scripts/asm_file.py`). DESIGN.md, "Kernel-checked compiler output".
    21  -/

== ConAgua/AsmFile/Include.lean#L8-L27
     8  # `include_asm "path"`: an assembler file as a `Program` (TRUSTED)
     9  
    10  `include_asm "path"` is a term of type `Program`: the `.text` section of the assembler file at
    11  `path` (relative to the directory of the current Lean file, as `include_str`), read by
    12  `parseAsmFile` (`ConAgua/AsmFile/Parse.lean`) when the term is elaborated, and turned into a term by
    13  `programTerm` (`ConAgua/AsmFile/Term.lean`). A file it cannot parse is an error.
    14  
    15  The term is cut into segments for the kernel's sake, without changing its value: a new segment
    16  starts at the label `ca_enter` (the trampoline) and at each function entry `ca_f_g`; the labels of
    17  segment `ca_f_g` are written as `lbl "g" n m` where that is their value. So the term is
    18  `stub ++ (trampoline ++ (f₀ ++ (… ++ (fₖ ++ []))))`, the shape `asm_lit`'s `checkerAsm` has.
    19  
    20  The trusted base is this parser (`parseAsmFile`): the term comes from it alone. Two independent
    21  cross-checks, not needed for soundness: Kraken's own parser must read the file's code the same way
    22  (`ConAgua/AsmFile/CrossCheck.lean`, run by `scripts/asm_file.py`: ~13 s, too slow to
    23  run here), and the assembler must encode what the file says (`scripts/check-asm.sh`). And here,
    24  the code is printed again with Kraken's printer (`toATT`) and compared with the file's `.text`
    25  lines: parse ∘ print is the identity on the file, so the parser reads every instruction the way
    26  the printer (which wrote the file) meant it.
    27  

== ConAgua/AsmFile/CrossCheck.lean#L5-L11
     5  /-! `lake env lean --run ConAgua/AsmFile/CrossCheck.lean FILE.s`: reads the file's code with both
     6  parsers, the trusted one (`parseAsmFile`, `ConAgua/AsmFile/Parse.lean`, which the final theorems'
     7  term comes from) and Kraken's own (`Kraken.X64.Parser.parse`, independent code), and fails
     8  (exit 1), naming the first differing directive, its line and function, if they disagree. A
     9  cross-check, not part of the trusted base; `scripts/asm_file.py` runs it. It is
    10  not in `include_asm`: Kraken's parser takes about 17 s on the checker's 5.3 MB there, twice the
    11  module's elaboration time (docs/design/asmfile.md). -/

== scripts/asm_file.py#L2-L21
     2  """Regenerate the two committed generated files the binary is built from (`make`, `Makefile`):
     3  
     4  * `checker.s`: the entry stub, the trampoline and the compiled checker, printed by
     5    `ConAgua/Checker/AsmEmit.lean` (run as a script, so the compiler runs as compiled Lean code;
     6    nothing here is trusted: the final theorems are about the file as the trusted parser reads it
     7    (`ConAguaAsm/Checker.lean`), and the kernel checks that it is the compiler's output,
     8    `checkerFile_eq` in `ConAgua/Checker/AsmFileEq.lean`). Regenerate after every change to the
     9    checker's L code (`ConAgua/Checker/Prog.lean`), the compiler or the stub.
    10  * `pins.bin`: the pin data `main.c` embeds, written by `romgen pins.bin 3`
    11    (`ConAgua/Rom/Gen.lean`): the checker's startup data and all of con-leche's `natOpPinSets` (3
    12    variants, the set con-ron embeds). Not trusted either: the theorems hold for every pin buffer.
    13    Regenerate after a change to the startup data or a twin bump.
    14  
    15  Both modes also run the parser cross-check `ConAgua/AsmFile/CrossCheck.lean` on `checker.s`:
    16  Kraken's own parser must read the code as the trusted parser does (~13 s; not in `include_asm`,
    17  where it would double the module's elaboration time).
    18  
    19  Usage: scripts/asm_file.py [--check] [--no-build]
    20    --check     fail (exit 1) if a file would change; do not write it
    21    --no-build  do not build ConAgua.Checker.AsmEmit's imports and romgen first"""

== ConAgua/Rom/Gen.lean#L13-L22
    13  def main (args : List String) : IO UInt32 := do
    14    let some out := args.head? | IO.eprintln "usage: romgen OUT [N]"; return 2
    15    let k := ((args.drop 1).head?.bind String.toNat?).getD 1
    16    let pins := ConLeche.natOpPinSets.take k
    17    let t0 ← IO.monoMsNow
    18    let bytes := pinBuffer pins
    19    IO.FS.writeBinFile out (ByteArray.mk bytes.toArray)
    20    let t1 ← IO.monoMsNow
    21    IO.println s!"{out}: {bytes.length} bytes ({romData.length} startup data, {pins.length} variant(s)), {t1 - t0} ms"
    22    return 0

== ConAgua/Final/TwinPooled.lean#L3-L13
     3  /-!
     4  # The twin's pipeline with phase B as con-ron's pool (lane parmode)
     5  
     6  The threaded mode checks the pending groups on several workers; what its accept means on the twin
     7  side is con-ron's `PooledAccepts` (`ConRon/Arena/Pooled.lean`): phase A accepted, and a family of
     8  group lists covering every pending group, each accepted by `checkPendingList` from the phase-A
     9  state's worker. `TwinAcceptsPooled` is `TwinAccepts` with that phase B; `TwinAccepts` is the pool
    10  with one part (`TwinAccepts.pooled`). Its consequences (con-leche's pure fold, the model, no
    11  theorem of type `False`) are `Twin.lean`'s, through Theorem 1 for the pool
    12  (`Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge`), which is what `twinAccepts_pure` already uses.
    13  (Lane parallel's `Twin.lean` changes, as a separate file.)

== ConAgua/Checker/Entry.lean#L126-L141
   126  /-- `check_b()`: on the worker region's first call the seed (`CTL`) from the buffer, then the
   127  pending groups `PLO‥PHI-1` (`PHI` at most the count) at phase A's final view, in order, as phase
   128  B's loop (`check_pending_go`); returns `ACCEPT`. -/
   129  -- con-ron: ConRon/Arena/Phased.lean:29-36 ConRon.Arena.AState.worker

   131  def checkBL : FunDecl := lfn () locals (z, n) {
   132    if INIT == 0 {
   133      n := len(CTLF.u64);
   134      copy!(CTL.u64, 0, CTLF.u64, 0, n);
   135      INIT := 1
   136    };
   137    if CTL.u64[130] < PHI { abort };
   138    if PHI < PLO { abort };
   139    z := call check_pending_go(PLO, PHI, HDRF.u64[3]);
   140    return 71757147230292
   141  }

== ConAgua/Compiler/Abi.lean#L210-L219
   210  * `ca_start(in, in_len, pins, pins_len, base, base_len)` (**the sequential driver**, what the
   211    harness calls): entry 1 with the mode word `3` (`ca_start_a0`: the buffer's header only); if it
   212    returns `rdx = 0` and `rax = 2^63 + k`, `ca_check_seq` on the same region for `[0, k)`, whose
   213    result is the result. It needs no more memory than `ca_setup`: entry 2 runs on phase A's region,
   214    on the arrays as phase A left them.
   215    It keeps its return address and the caller's `r15` past `ca_setup`'s region (`drvSave`; the
   216    driver's region is 16 bytes larger, `drvNeed`, the size `ca_region_size` names), pops its return
   217    address off the machine stack before each `call` and holds `base` in `r15` (which `ca_enter`
   218    restores); so each callee's machine stack is the caller's (the 32 bytes `AbiCall` names) and
   219    the driver touches no callee-saved register but `r15`. -/

== main.c#L168-L186
   168  /* `--jobs=N` (N > 1), the threaded mode.
   169  
   170     Entry 1 (`ca_start_a`) runs the stages and phase A in the region. On success (rdx = 0,
   171     rax = 2^63 + k, k pending groups) it has written the frozen buffer into the array `OUT`, whose
   172     word 1 is the buffer's length in words. The buffer stays where it is: the rest of the region is
   173     unmapped around it and the buffer is made read-only, so a write to it faults and kills the
   174     process, which is never an accept (route A). N threads then each map their own zero region of
   175     ca_worker_size bytes and claim group indices from one atomic counter, calling
   176     `ca_check_b(buf, len, j, region, region_len)` for each claimed j, one call after the other on
   177     the region as the previous call left it.
   178  
   179     Concurrency: the threads share only the read-only buffer, the claim counter (fetch_add hands
   180     out each of 0, 1, 2, ... once) and a stop flag that only shortens a failing run. Each thread
   181     has its own region and its own result slot; main combines the slots after joining every
   182     thread. Accept iff no slot holds a failure: every call that thread made accepted, and the
   183     threads drain the counter past k unless one fails. Otherwise the verdict is that of the
   184     failing group with the smallest index, as a one-thread run would report it: the indices are
   185     claimed in order and a thread finishes the group it holds, so every lower group has been
   186     checked, and accepted, when the threads are joined. */

    55  | D30 | `Checker/Hoist.lean` `hoist_nat_op_ground` | `applyHoist` also returns the moved records' names (`movedNames`, the `hoisted` receipt of `prepareD`) | not computed | none (`preparePrelude` drops the receipt) | front3 | by design: the result is never read |
    56  | D31 | `Checker/Prelude.lean` `builtin_prelude`, `front_reset`, `preFn` | `builtinPreludeE` runs `parseBytes preludeText` with a fresh `StateD`, keeps the records as a `PreludeIx` value; `parseChunks` then starts from a fresh `StateD` | the prelude's parse runs the frontend (input renamed to the constant `preludeBytes`) on the stream's own parse-state arrays; then only the id tables are reset (`front_reset`), the prelude's records stay in `DECL[0‥P)` and the stream's parse appends after them | none (same records, same stores; the twin's parse only pushes to `decls`) | pipeline | by design: the frontend's refinement applies to both parses unchanged, the prelude's copy differs from the frontend only in the input (`preSim`), and no copy of the records is needed |
    57  | D32 | `Arena/IndPos.lean` `nest_ctor_entry_strip` | `nestCtorEntry` passes `nPc + nF` (a `Nat` sum) to `stripPis` | aborts when the word sum `nPc + nF` wraps (a capacity guard) | none: never accepts more; cannot trigger on real inputs (both counts are word-sized field counts) | indstaget | by design: removes the environment-wide premise `CtorSums` from the positivity and recursor proofs |
    58  | D33 | `Arena/StubInd.lean` `open_pis_at_fvars_f` | `openPisAtFvarsF n e i` names its free variables `i, i + 1, …` (`Nat`s) | aborts when the first index `i` is `≥ 2^63` (a capacity guard: with at most the spine stack's `< 2^63` binders opened, the word indices `i + j` cannot wrap) | none: never accepts more; cannot trigger on real inputs (`i` is a binder depth) | indproofs4 | by design: discharges `opfF_ok`'s premise `i < 2^63` inside, so no depth bound reaches its callers |
    59  | D34 | `Arena/ConsLib.lean` `ciChk` (in `consInternG`): `intern_app`, `intern_lam`, `intern_forall`, `intern_const`, `intern_fvar`, `intern_max`, `intern_imax` | `internE`/`internL` hash-cons any key | aborts unless both key words are below `2^32` (an exact table's slot keeps the key packed in one word, `k₁ \| k₂ << 32`, and a probe compares it without reading the record) | none: `mk_app`/`mk_lam`/`mk_forall` already abort on larger words; a `const`/`fvar`/`max`/`imax` key is made of handle words (name, level list, level, expression; below `2^32` by construction, `consInternM_lt`) and an fvar index | kstp-proof | by design: the packed key word (lane kstp, `docs/design/conslib.md` step 4) |
    60  | D36 | `Arena/ConsLib.lean` `kfHead`, `kpickB`; `Arena/MemoLib.lean` `memoFindG`, `mslotBlkG` (`homeW`) | `ron/hashmap2.rs` `home_index`: `mix(h) & (n - 1)` | `mulhi(mix(h), n)` (the top bits of the mixed hash) | none (the home is verdict-neutral; hashmap2.rs says so) | memlay | stays: with our key hashes the mask clusters (lane memlay, phase 1: let-ladder's scratch tier probes 3.30 slots per find with the mask, 1.82 with `mulhi`, both at load 3/4) |
    61  | D38 | `Arena/ConsLib.lean` `kgrowB` (`kmarkL`, `krehashL`: in-place growth) | `ron/hashmap2.rs` `try_resize`: a new table of twice the capacity, the live slots moved into it, the old `Vec` freed | the table doubles where it is: the upper half zeroed, the live slots marked, each marked entry re-inserted (absl's in-place rehash for linear probing) | none (representation only; no old copy stays resident, which L could not free) | memlay | stays: L has no allocator to give the old table back |

== docs/deviations.md#L63-L90
    63  ## Fixed
    64  
    65  - **D4** (fixed by lane consync, helper consync-pins): con-ron ed864140 retired `orElseAttempt` (its task #129): an error inside a pin-variant attempt is the run's error in the twin too, and L's loop is the twin's boolean decision loop (`check_div_mod_pin_loop`); the attempt flag `ATT` and the `fail R` class masking are gone.
    66  - **D21, D22, D29** (fixed by lane consync, the twin bump to con-ron `ed864140`): the projection tables left the constants (con-leche task #362): no reserved table name is interned any more (`proj_table_name` is gone; tables are keyed on the structure name in the environment's table component, `find_table`), and no constant is a projection table (the ROM reader has no kind `6` to refuse).
    67  - **D39** (fixed by lane epochwrap): `scratch_reset` aborted after `2^30` resets (the slot base `B = CTL[62]` at `2^62`); now at `B ≥ 2^62` it vacates the 19 scratch slot tables (the growth's zero loop `kzeroLs`) and restarts `B` at `0`, as con-ron's `HashMap2::clear` at `EPOCH_MAX` (docs/design/epochwrap.md).
    68  - **D35** (fixed by lane tierswitch): every store keeps one word array per tier (tier `t` of array `a` is the word array `tierA a t`, `ld64t`/`st64t`): records `ra⟨t⟩[i * w + f]`, slot tables `sa⟨t⟩` (one KSTP formula per tier array), derived and level-parameter columns `col⟨t⟩[i]`, as con-ron's per-tier `Tbl`s (docs/design/tierswitch.md).
    69  - **D1** (fixed by decls3 landing 4 and lane integrate): `and_pin_ok`'s inductive arm landed (kind `6`) and `rom_and_pin` got L code, so the real `And` block is accepted.
    70  - **F1** (fixed by lane twinaudit): id tables dense + sparse (`IdTable`); ids past the end no longer abort (`e2e/rounds_huge_gaps`).
    71  - **F2** (fixed by lane front2): strings with escapes (`Unescape.lean`, `str_put_esc`).
    72  - **F3** (fixed by lane strlit): `strVal` lines.
    73  - **F4** (fixed by `nat_dec`, `ApplyExpr.lean`): `natVal` past 18 digits.
    74  - **F5** (fixed by lane front2): expression and declaration lines.
    75  - **F6** (fixed by lanes indproofs/indproofs2, landing 6): inductive lines in the front.
    76  - **F7** (fixed by lane romload): pin data as an input.
    77  - **F8** (fixed by lane decls): the readback's `EMemo` mirrored with back references.
    78  - **F9** (fixed by lane decls3): uncached `lvl_eq` in lane induct's code, now `lvl_eq_c`.
    79  - **F10** (fixed by lane whnf): the eager mode-memo take/put banks, via the eager key bit.
    80  - **F11** (fixed by lane libs): dropping the scratch tier cost O(capacity); epoch slots.
    81  - **F12** (fixed in place by lanes indproofs, decls2, indproofs2): `sl_get` out of range, `check_block_agree` on an empty rest, `pin_in` on an empty table, `class_read` wrapping.
    82  - **F13** (fixed by lane whnf2): uncached `lvls_eq` in `iota_rec_at`, now `lvls_eq_c`.
    83  - **F14** (fixed by lane indproofs2): uncached `lvls_eq` in `target_class_match` (was D7), now `lvls_eq_c`.
    84  - **F15** (fixed by helper whnf4-d23): D23, `lp_go`/`inst_lp_core` could not cut off at a parameter-free node (L's derived words kept only the two ranges), so the walk descended into parameter-free subterms and `inst_lp_core` read `ls_node(us)` for a parameter-free `e`. Now the level-parameter bit is mirrored per node (`LpCol.lean`: bit 30 of the five `XDER` words; columns 55‥61 for `succ`/`max`/`imax`/level lists/`sort`/`const`/`fvar`, written when the node is pushed; `ArenaR`'s `*Hp`/`*Lp` fields, `DerR`'s `bvP`/`zlP`), read by `der_b`'s third result (`derLW_ok`), and `lp_go`/`inst_lp_core` test it first, as `instLPGo`/`instLPFast`.
    85  - **F16** (fixed by lane defeq2): D25, `lvl_live` checked `imax` arguments with `lv_node` (a level read before a knot call was not known to read back after it). Now `PoolGrew.lvl` (the level tables only grow) rides in `CoreAfter` and `lvl_den_later` reads the level back; L mirrors the twin again.
    86  - **F17** (lane slotgrow): the cons tables (`SLOT` … `NNSLOT`) were fixed at their whole array and `X_push` aborted at 3/4 load; now they grow like con-ron's `HashMap2` (double and rehash, here at 1/2 load from 8 slots per tier, `SlotGrow.lean`), so a large slot array no longer costs memory or page faults up front.
    87  - **D18/D24** (`hoist_ok`, fixed by lane front3): the ground hoist `hoistNatOpGround` in L (`Checker/Hoist.lean`); `prepare_prelude` reorders instead of aborting (`e2e/natop_order`, `natop_before_ble`).
    88  - **F18** (lane memlay): the cons tables and the memos grew at load 1/2 (no row had recorded it); now at 3/4, con-ron's `HashMap2` load factor (`LOAD_NUM/LOAD_DEN`).
    89  - **D5** (fixed by lane harness): the harness loaded a 1-variant pin buffer; the binary now embeds `pins.bin` = `romgen pins.bin 3`, all three of con-leche's `natOpPinSets` variants, as con-ron embeds them (18 more e2e accepts, none lost).
    90  - **D41** (retired by lane scanfast-p3): `fast_line`, a recogniser of lean4export's canonical byte form tried before the generic scanner, coupled the checker to the exporter's exact output; the single pass `line_rec` (`Front/LineRec.lean`) reads each line once, in any member order and spacing, as con-ron's `scan_line_loop` does.

== scripts/e2e.py#L2-L25
     2  """End-to-end differential testing of the L checker (lane `e2e`, DESIGN.md "End-to-end runs").
     3  
     4  Steps (all in _tmp/e2e/<checkout name>/):
     5  
     6  1. **Assemble.** Every `ConAgua` module (except executables and the spike) is imported, in as few
     7     import closures as the modules allow (some clash on declaration names; each clash is reported),
     8     and `ConAgua/E2E/Dump.lean` dumps every binding of an L function name to a FunDecl it finds
     9     (`Prog` lists and `p.lookup "f" = some d` hypotheses). The bindings are merged; the program is
    10     everything reachable from `check` and `check_np` (`ConAgua/E2E/Check.lean`). A called function
    11     with no L code (no binding, or only `abort` stubs) gets an e2e stub with its own code.
    12  2. **Compile.** `check`: the shipped code, printed by `checker.s`'s generator
    13     (`ConAgua/Checker/AsmEmit.lean`; the report says whether the committed file is up to date);
    14     `check_np`: `e2e-l asm` (checks `Prog.wf`). Each linked with `cc main.c` (the entry stub
    15     lays out a fixed partition of one region, lane `abi`: no capacity retries).
    16  3. **Run** every fixture (con-leche's e2e fixtures and the arena tests) through the compiled
    17     `check` and `check_np`, the reference `e2e-ref` (the twin at the program's pin list; with and
    18     without the prelude), and `L.run` (`e2e-l run`) on small fixtures; classify.
    19  4. **Report** `docs/e2e.md` (and `--csv` appends a line to `docs/e2e.csv`).
    20  
    21  Never a merge gate. Every run has a timeout; a monitor kills any run above PER_RUN_GB and the
    22  largest run while all together are above TOTAL_GB.
    23  
    24  Usage: scripts/e2e.py [--no-build] [--jobs N] [--only REGEX] [--rerun-failing [RESULTS]]
    25                       [--trace {disagree,all,none}] [--trace-sample N] [--write] [--csv]

== scripts/diff-e2e.py#L2-L44
     2  """The end-to-end differential of the shipped binary: `./checker FILE.ndjson` on every fixture of
     3  con-leche's test suite that has a pinned expectation, against that expectation. No Lean needed.
     4  
     5      scripts/diff-e2e.py [--bin PATH] [--jobs N] [--parallel P] [--timeout S] [--tests DIR] [--only REGEX]
     6                          [--refs] [--no-cache]
     7  
     8  The fixtures and the expected exit codes are con-leche's `tests/` at the revision `vendor/UPSTREAM`
     9  pins: `tests/e2e-expected.txt` ("<exit> <fixture>" under `tests/e2e/`, gzipped or not) and
    10  `tests/arena-expected.txt` ("<exit> <path>" inside `tests/arena/lean-arena-tests.tar.gz`).
    11  con-leche's exit codes are 0 accept, 1 reject, 2 decline, 3 error, 124 a deliberate non-terminating
    12  input. `--tests` names that directory (default `$CON_LECHE_TESTS`, else the tests at exactly the pinned
    13  revision, extracted from the reference clone `_tmp/ref/con-leche` with `git archive` into
    14  `_tmp/ref/con-leche-tests/<rev>/` by `scripts/conleche_tests.py`, fetching if needed; the clone's
    15  working tree is never used). An override is not checked against the pin.
    16  
    17  The checker exits 0 only on accept, 1 on a reject, 2 on a decline, 3 otherwise (`main.c`'s usage
    18  text). Its reject/decline labels follow con-ron's twin, not con-leche, so a fixture is compared on
    19  accept versus not-accept, and a reject/decline that differs from con-leche's is only counted
    20  (`kind differs`):
    21    agree         con-leche accepts and the checker accepts, or con-leche does not accept and the
    22                  checker exits 1, 2 or 3 (a run still going after T_LOOP seconds counts here when
    23                  con-leche's expectation is the non-terminating 124)
    24    UNSOUND       the checker accepts where con-leche does not
    25    INCOMPLETE    con-leche accepts and the checker exits 1, 2 or 3
    26    CRASH         a signal, or an exit code the checker never uses
    27    TIMEOUT       the run did not finish in `--timeout` seconds (and 124 was not expected)
    28  The run is green when every fixture agrees; the exit code is 0 then, 1 otherwise (2: usage, missing
    29  fixtures).
    30  
    31  `--refs` also runs con-ron (`--jobs=1`) and `e2e-ref` on every fixture and reports REFDIFF where either
    32  one's accept/not-accept differs from the checker's, or where the checker rejects or declines and con-ron
    33  does not say the same (the full differential of PLAN.md's "Verdict checks");
    34  it replaces `bench.py --reps 0`, which no longer checks verdicts. The references' verdicts depend only
    35  on the fixture and the reference binary, so they are cached in `_tmp/bench/verdict-cache/`, keyed by the
    36  fixture's content hash and the hash of the reference binary (and, for con-ron, its pins file): after the
    37  first run, `--refs` costs about as much as the plain run, until a twin sync changes a binary. Timeouts are
    38  never cached. A fixture expecting 124 gets T_LOOP seconds on every system.
    39  (`--no-cache` ignores the cache.) Needs the references built as `scripts/bench.py` does (`.lake/build/bin/e2e-ref`,
    40  con-ron at `$CON_RON` or `_tmp/ref/con-ron-integrate/target/release/con-ron`).
    41  
    42  `--jobs N` is passed to the checker (`--jobs=N`, the threaded mode; 1, the default, passes nothing
    43  and runs the sequential path). `--parallel P` is how many fixtures run at once (default 4).
    44  """

== scripts/gates.sh#L11-L23
    11  # Steps, in order (stops at the first failure):
    12  #   links       scripts/overview-links.sh            OVERVIEW.md/README.md line anchors
    13  #   vendor      scripts/bump-con-ron.sh --check      vendor/ = upstream + patches
    14  #   modules     scripts/modules_check.py             every module is built by a target
    15  #   provenance  scripts/provenance.py check          every FunDecl's twin citation is exact
    16  #   reasons     scripts/reasons.py --check           (when the script exists)
    17  #   build       scripts/lake build ConAgua           (timeout 90 min)
    18  #   warnings    scripts/lean_warnings.py --base BASE   no Lean warning in the changed .lean files (vendor/
    19  #               excluded), also for modules restored from the shared cache (their logs are in the log store)
    20  #   shake       scripts/shake.py                     every import `lake shake` finds unused is allowlisted
    21  #   core-fns, loop-fns, leaf-fns, preloop-ws         the generated call closures are current
    22  #   checker-prog  scripts/checker_prog.py --no-build --check   the generated program files are current
    23  #   e2e         make checker; scripts/diff-e2e.py --parallel 16   verdicts on every fixture

== .github/workflows/ci.yml#L4-L76
     4  # WHAT THE JOBS COVER
     5  #
     6  #   checker  The shipped binary, with no Lean anywhere (a few minutes):
     7  #              make, make check   `main.c` + `checker.s` + `pins.bin` build
     8  #                                 with a C23 compiler (`#embed`), and the
     9  #                                 smoke test passes (the prelude is
    10  #                                 accepted, a malformed line is not).
    11  #              scripts/diff-e2e.py  the end-to-end differential: the built
    12  #                                 `checker` on every fixture of
    13  #                                 con-leche's test suite that has a pinned
    14  #                                 expectation (628: `tests/e2e/` and the
    15  #                                 arena snapshot), against that
    16  #                                 expectation, compared on accept versus
    17  #                                 not-accept (the checker exits 0 only on
    18  #                                 accept, and does not tell a reject from a
    19  #                                 decline).  Green is every fixture
    20  #                                 agreeing: no accept where con-leche does
    21  #                                 not accept, no non-accept where it
    22  #                                 accepts, no crash, no timeout.  Two
    23  #                                 lanes: the sequential path (the default
    24  #                                 run) and `--jobs=4` (the threaded mode),
    25  #                                 which must give the same verdicts.
    26  #            The fixtures are con-leche's own `tests/`, checked out at the
    27  #            revision `vendor/UPSTREAM` pins (sparse: `tests/` only).
    28  #
    29  #   proof    The proofs and every gate that guards the committed files:
    30  #              overview-links.sh  every line-anchored link of OVERVIEW.md
    31  #                                 and README.md still cites the recorded
    32  #                                 lines (no build);
    33  #              modules_check.py   every `ConAgua/**` module is built by
    34  #                                 some target (no build);
    35  #              bump-con-ron.sh --check  `vendor/` is exactly the upstream
    36  #                                 files at `vendor/UPSTREAM` plus
    37  #                                 `vendor/patches/` (clones con-ron and
    38  #                                 con-leche into `_tmp/ref/`);
    39  #              provenance.py check  every L function's twin citation is
    40  #                                 exact at the vendored revisions;
    41  #              scripts/lake build  the default targets: L, the compiler,
    42  #                                 the checker, every proof, the vendored
    43  #                                 con-leche and con-ron.  This includes
    44  #                                 the axiom guards (`#guard_msgs` on the
    45  #                                 final theorems' `#print axioms`), the
    46  #                                 kernel's check that `checker.s` is the
    47  #                                 compiler's output (`checkerFile_eq`) and
    48  #                                 the staleness checks of the generated
    49  #                                 call closures;
    50  #              check-no-warnings.sh  the build's log holds no warning
    51  #                                 outside Kraken (a Lake dependency);
    52  #              shake.py           every import Lean's import minimizer
    53  #                                 (`lake shake`) finds unused is on
    54  #                                 `scripts/shake-allowlist.txt`;
    55  #              the `--check` modes of the generators: asm_file.py
    56  #                                 (`checker.s` and `pins.bin` are what the
    57  #                                 generators print now, plus Kraken's own
    58  #                                 parser reading `checker.s` as the
    59  #                                 trusted parser does), core_fns.py,
    60  #                                 loop_fns.py, leaf_fns.py, preloop_ws.py.
    61  #
    62  # WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES **NOT** COVER
    63  #
    64  #   * the differential against the two reference checkers
    65  #     (`scripts/e2e.py`: con-ron's arena checker compiled by Lean, and
    66  #     con-ron's Rust binary), and its interpreter and per-function
    67  #     sweeps: they need a Rust build of con-ron and Lean executables
    68  #     on top of the proof build, and take far longer than the verdict
    69  #     sweep above, which already compares every fixture with the
    70  #     pinned expectation.
    71  #   * `scripts/bench.py` and the `Init` benchmark: an export of `Init`
    72  #     is not in the repository, and a shared runner measures noise.
    73  #     Timings are measured with `perf stat` on a quiet machine.
    74  #   * the progress census (`scripts/census.py`) and the build
    75  #     statistics: reports, not gates.
    76  #

>>> README.md
